FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Section Twelve offers an eleven-item multiple-choice rehearsal with three options per item and a closing answer key, inviting readers to test themselves before the real exam [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
The opening item probes impairment, whose correct lesson is that alcohol and drugs corrode judgment rather than quickening reactions or sharpening focus [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
A dashed yellow line on your side alone opens passing on your side only [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Twin arrivals at a four-way stop resolve by yielding to the right-hand driver [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Two picture items quiz sign reading, one for the divided-highway-ahead warning and one for curve signage [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
Regulatory signs wear white, not green or yellow [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
Mid-street jaywalkers still command a stop despite their illegality [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
Motorcycle operators own a complete traffic lane, never a shared lane or the shoulder [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A01
Cyclists earn slow speeds and maximum passing room, never horns or hurried squeezes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A01
High beams belong to empty roads, never to fog, rain, snow, or followers [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A01
Distraction means anything dragging attention from driving itself [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A01
A compact letter key scores all eleven rehearsal items at the section's foot [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A02
The closing page credits an AAMVA distracted-driving whitepaper, federal visual-manual distraction guidelines, and a Virginia Tech distraction study [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A02
The imprint dates the manual to 2022 under the American Association of Motor Vehicle Administrators of Arlington, Virginia, frames it as a rules-and-signs supplement, and credits motorcycle-safety and highway-safety artwork [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0081]
